question: What will the IEA's November 2026 Oil Market Report say about the change in world oil demand in 2026 (y/y, mb/d)?

calls.reasoning: Anchor: October OMR -2.6 mb/d (Q2 -5.0, Q3 -3.7, Q4 -2.5). The downgrade sequence (-1.1,-1.0,-1.6,-2.5,-2.6) has slowed, and late in the year only Q4 has meaningful leverage over the annual figure. October saw Hormuz attacks double and end-month flows collapse, with Brent up 13% to ~$117, so the skew is toward a further small downgrade. But the IEA already allowed for renewed attacks in October, and prices may have eased from ~$134 Dated when that report was written. No human market was found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi. Median -2.65, skewed slightly downward.
calls.dossier:
- IEA Oct 2026 OMR (pub 14 Oct): 2026 world demand 102.4 mb/d, -2.6 mb/d y/y; Q2 -5.0, Q3 -3.7, Q4 -2.5 mb/d y/y (these imply Q1 is about +0.8). Diesel is ~25% of the loss. Source: Argus/globaltradingoutlook, Oct 2026.
- Oct OMR reportedly left rest-of-year projections largely unchanged despite renewed October attacks; North Sea Dated was ~$134/bbl when the report was written, with a September average of $116.89 (globaltradingoutlook).
- Path of the IEA 2026 growth figure: Jun -1.1, Jul -1.0, Aug -1.6, Sep -2.5, Oct -2.6 (question background).
- Gulf crude exports rose 4.4 mb/d in Sep to 13.9 mb/d; total Hormuz flows in Sep were 10.9 mb/d (globaltradingoutlook, Oct).
- CNBC 30 Oct 2026: Hormuz crude exports averaged ~11.1 mb/d in Oct (-2% vs Sep), but the final week fell to 7.3 mb/d; at least 30 vessels were attacked in Oct vs 15 in Sep; tanker freight went from $6.50 to $21/bbl; Brent rose >13% in Oct to >$117, near the March peak of $118.35.
- straits.live 3 Nov 2026: strait described as effectively closed; IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on 25 Oct vs a baseline of ~85/day; Iran says it could reopen within 2 days if the US meets its conditions; Brent settled at $113.43 on the last Friday.
- Sensitivity: a 1 mb/d change to Q4 y/y moves the annual figure by ~0.25 mb/d; revisions to Q3 from Sep/Oct data also feed in.
- Cross-agency figures (IEF Oct): OPEC +0.2, EIA -2.0, IEA -2.6 mb/d.
- Status quo: the Nov OMR repeats -2.6.
- Resolves off the IEA Nov 2026 OMR overview/highlights figure for full-year 2026 y/y (one decimal; kb/d is converted), not quarterly figures or other agencies.
- Event window: single publication on 13 Nov 2026; as of 3 Nov, the Oct-Nov inter-report interval is ~67% elapsed.
- Searched but not found: Kalshi/Polymarket/Manifold markets on the IEA figure; full text of the Oct OMR (IEA page returned 403); any preview of the Nov OMR.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the factual base (Oct OMR -2.6, quarterly split, October escalation, Iran's reopening offer, no markets) and on a median of -2.65 with a downside skew. No factual disputes needed settling; the only difference was width (0.5 vs 0.65), a judgment call about how much Q4 or baseline revisions can move a ~10/12 in-sample annual figure. I kept a width of about 0.6 because baseline/Q3 data revisions are a real channel beyond Q4 leverage. No web retrieval on this run.
